page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.large is a high-clock-speed virtual instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.3 GHz. The instance provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core across 2 threads, supported by 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Cache infrastructure includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. Advanced instruction set extensions are available, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16.

The ecs.hfg7.large instance does not include local disk storage or integrated GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating the use of network-attached block storage for persistence. Network connectivity operates at a baseline throughput of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the instance by default.

Performance benchmarks reflect the single-core strength of the 3.3 GHz Intel architecture alongside the constraints of a single physical core. Single-threaded metrics fall in the middle 50% percentile across all tested hardware, registering 1308.0 on Geekbench single-core, 1571.88 on stress-ng single-core, and 26.79 GB/sec on gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core and system throughput metrics rank in the lower percentiles due to limited parallel compute capacity, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 1575.0, PassMark CPU scoring 2531.07, and Redis processing 2.03 million SET operations per second. Large-block memory throughput reaches 15.65 GB/sec for reads and 13.17 GB/sec for writes.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the ecs.hfg7.large provides a low-entry footprint with dedicated CPU execution, avoiding noisy neighbor contention on processing threads. Given the minimal vCPU count and reliance on network storage, it is suited for single-threaded processing scripts, lightweight background workers, development and testing environments, and low-traffic microservices.

It delivers 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads, 8.0 GB of RAM, and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU acceleration, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Architectural extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates moderate single-threaded capability, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 1308.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 26.79 GB/sec. Due to its limited physical core count, multi-core and memory throughput metrics fall into lower tiers, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 1575.0. This configuration offers predictable thread execution for lightweight enterprise applications, microservices, continuous integration tasks, and single-threaded processing tasks requiring moderate memory and consistent CPU frequency.
